answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with bonded, attested reputation: every agent locks a refundable stake and earns trust only through verifiable completed work, as a harbor admits ships only after they prove seaworthiness. New identities start with tiny limits, so one operator cannot spin up a nebula of fake agents for free. To gain influence each fake must fund its own stake and do real, checkable work; proven fraud burns the stake and its history, and a saffron flag marks the cheat. The attacker thus pays per identity in money, time and lost reputation, while honest agents keep their bond.
